title: Session orphan rehabilitation and adaptive backoff for disconnected streaming clients
creator: Aisha Khan
description: When clients disconnect mid-stream (network flaps, tab closes, mobile backgrounding) we currently either hold resources indefinitely or immediately evict state, both of which cause suboptimal UX and cost. This ticket defines a rehabilitative flow that: 1) maintains a short, observable 'rehab' window for disconnected sessions to resume; 2) introduces an adaptive backoff for client reconnect attempts and retries to avoid thundering-herd on recoverable sessions; 3) reclaims KV/prefix cache and ephemeral allocations deterministically after a configurable compact grace period; and 4) emits fine-grained metrics and traces for debugging partial-generation states. The goal is to reduce wasted compute and customer-visible partial outputs while enabling quick client resume when appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable rehab window (default 60s) honored: disconnected sessions remain resumable during window
Adaptive reconnect backoff implemented on server-side with jitter and client guidance headers
KV/prefix caches tied to session epoch and compacted deterministically after rehab + compact grace windows
End-to-end integration tests cover: resume within window, resume after resume-window (fails), repeated flapping clients, and large-scale reconnect storm simulation
New dashboard tile shows active rehab sessions, reclamation rate, and reconnect storms; SLO alert if reclaim queue grows > 5 min backlog
Documentation added in Console runbooks and API docs: headers, response codes, recovery tokens and recommended client retry strategy
tech_notes: Design: assign each streaming session a short-lived epoch token (rehab_token) persisted to lightweight metadata store; token is redeemable during rehab window to reattach session state
Adaptive backoff: server returns Retry-After and Retry-Jitter headers; algorithm = min( base * 2^n, max_backoff ) with randomized jitter in [0.75,1.25]
KV eviction: add session_epoch to kv cache keys; eviction runs in two phases: soft-compact (reclaim large prefixes) at rehab_end, hard-evict at rehab_end + compact_grace
Metrics: rehab.session.start, rehab.session.resume, rehab.session.evict, rehab.reclaim.duration, rehab.reconnect.storm_count tagged by model, region, customer_tier

Failure modes: if backend node dies and session cannot be attached, return structured partial-output token and stable resume failure message; clients should fallback to fresh generation using prefix cache hints
Trade-offs: longer rehab_window improves UX but increases memory; propose default 60s for hosted tier, 15s for burstable/dedicated to reduce cost footprint
Compat shim: for older SDKs without rehab_token support, server accepts tag-based resume using client-provided connection_id for up to 5s only; encourage SDK upgrade
Testing: use fault-injection harness to simulate TCP reset, NAT mappings change, and client replay at scale; include chaos test with 10k simulated connections
